core_obligations: Let Z be the reduction of X and apply the reduced case to obtain an ample invertible sheaf on Z (proof lines 8170-8172).
Use the lifting lemma for invertible modules along a closed immersion in dimension at most one to find an invertible O_X-module L whose restriction to Z is that ample sheaf (proof lines 8173-8175).
Deduce that L itself is ample on X from ampleness of its restriction to the reduction (proof lines 8176-8177).
proof_roadmap: Lift the ample sheaf from the reduction to the scheme.
Transfer ampleness back from the reduction.
difficulty_reason: The proposition proves that a Noetherian separated scheme of dimension at most one has an ample invertible sheaf, without any reducedness or integrality hypothesis. The proof splits the problem along the reduction: on the reduction Z the ample sheaf exists by the reduced case, it is then lifted to an invertible module L on the whole of X using the lifting lemma for closed immersions in dimension at most one, and finally ampleness of L is deduced from ampleness of its restriction to the reduction (proof lines 8170-8177). H3: the passage from the reduction to the scheme itself combines three independent results, and the lift step is exactly where the dimension hypothesis is used.

Difference in proof: the integral special case constructs the ample sheaf directly from an affine covering, while this proposition goes through the reduction and lifts the ample sheaf; the two arguments are therefore not the same proof of the same statement.
